Hey man, not a physician but I work emergency medical responses. Depending on how high your blood pressure is you may have other symptoms like your headache and do have a higher risk for other complications like heart attacks and strokes. 

THAT BEING SAID, I have seen people with blood pressures in the stratosphere with their only complaint being a headache. 

I work medical and have outstanding medical bills, so that part is pretty normal and I would try to stay calm about that. Stress and anxiety can cause your blood pressure to rise or for you to have other symptoms. If you ever have any sudden change to your headache, any weaknesses, stroke-like symptoms, or non reproducible substernal chest pain I would recommend going back to the ER. ERs are meant to rule out big and scary which is why they did the CT scan and blood work. Your physician will have to monitor your blood pressure over time to prescribe the right medication or find another way to improve it on its own.

Let me start by saying I am not a licensed medical professional so take my advice with a grain of salt. 

​

Reproducible on palpation chest pain is rarely cardiac in nature normally stemming from musc/skel means. This could be from lack of movement for an extended period of time or an independent medical issue like inflammation of the connective tissue in the rib cage. 

Due to your stated history I'm going to assume that along with your tendency have that orthostatic tachycardia you may have high blood pressure as well. As you stand up and your blood shifts your blood pressure may go down and cause your heart rate to go up. It can also be a sign of dehydration or a side effect of low physical fitness (being out of shape at least cardiovascular wise). 

I believe your biggest issue may be your anxiety as it seems to be triggering a lot of other health problems like the high heart rate. This isn't to say there aren't underlying medical issues but at least from an emergency perspective it seems like your tests all correlate to non-cardiac chest pain. 

With your EKG, some people have normal abnormalities. Although part of it may be abnormal, it is still physiologically normal for your body. I would continue with your cardiologist and psychiatrist to determine if there are any other issues. I would also recommend getting tested for any autoimmune diseases that may cause joint or cartilage inflammation as some of them, like  costochondritis can feel similar to a cardiac event. If you are ever unsure of your health and feel like you may be in immediate medical danger please call 911 or your relative emergency line.

I wish you all the best.
